I will keep my land mostly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to use my 10.1 mu, my well water, and the labor my family can provide. I have farmed for 20 years, so I will not chase anything complicated. I will put 8.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.1 mu in cotton to spread risk and keep some cash income. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and three irrigations because I have well irrigation and I want stable grain yield. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and sow directly after wheat harvest with no-tillage to save time and keep the season tight. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it needs more pest control and more careful field work, but I still want it in my plan. I will use enough potassium on cotton, spray more often than on grain crops, and manage water carefully so I can hold a decent yield without overstretching my household labor.
